tools.name: Hangar
tools.description: Inspect Firefox CI fleet inventory, worker and pool health, alerts, and Puppet configuration in a shared dashboard.
tools.when_to_use: Use Hangar when you need a fleet-wide starting point for investigating worker health, load, or alerts. Start with the overview, then narrow to a platform, pool, or machine to inspect inventory and configuration.

default.prerequisites: A web browser and a Mozilla Google account with dashboard access. No local Python environment or Taskcluster token is needed.

tools.name: Pool Classifier
tools.description: Review Taskcluster pool health, task success rates, alerting workers, and failures grouped by log patterns.
tools.when_to_use: Start here when a worker pool's success rate changes and you want to see which workers or failures account for it. The dashboard groups task results using log patterns, helping you move from a pool-wide symptom to examples worth inspecting.

default.prerequisites: A web browser and a Mozilla Google account with dashboard access. No local Python environment or Taskcluster token is needed.

tools.name: Taskcluster Web Launcher
tools.description: Find Firefox CI worker pools and open their Taskcluster pages.
tools.when_to_use: Use this terminal picker when you know a worker pool name or part of one and want to reach its Taskcluster page quickly. Choose a pool to open it in your browser, or print its URL for use elsewhere.

beta.prerequisites: Python 3 with curses and SQLite support, GitHub SSH access, and an interactive terminal for the picker. Uses only the Python standard library; no uv, Pipenv, or Taskcluster token is needed. Fetching pool lists needs Firefox CI HTTPS access. Opening a selected URL also needs a browser; --print only prints it.

tools.name: Taskcluster pool replay
tools.description: Test a worker pool by replaying completed level-1 jobs from another pool, tracking workload coverage and available capacity.
tools.when_to_use: Use pool replay when testing a destination pool against a mix of jobs from an existing pool, for example while evaluating a worker configuration change. Coverage tracks which discovered workload types have completed successfully in the replay session, rather than treating one successful task as a full test.

beta.prerequisites: Python 3.11+, GitHub SSH access, and Pipenv for initial setup; relops installs the locked runtime dependencies. Active monitoring, including --dry-run, needs ~/.tc_token. Help and saved-session viewing need no Taskcluster credentials. Submission requires queue:create-task:lowest:DESTINATION (replace DESTINATION with the --queue pool), queue:create-task:project:none, queue:scheduler-id:-, and every scope requested by the selected source tasks. Workload-dependent grants are in the linked README; --help also lists common scopes.
beta.note: Monitoring starts with submissions paused; press S in the dashboard or pass --submit-on-start to enable them. Press P to inspect missing scopes. Use --session PATH to view a saved session without contacting Taskcluster, or --session PATH --resume --dry-run --once to check one monitoring cycle without submitting tasks.

tools.name: Taskcluster task replay
tools.description: Replay a completed level-1 Firefox CI task as an independent diagnostic task, or preview its task definition without submitting.
tools.when_to_use: Use task replay when one completed level-1 Firefox CI task provides a useful diagnostic workload for a worker pool. Preview its task definition before submitting an independent replay task; use pool replay when you need coverage across a mix of jobs.

beta.prerequisites: Python 3.11+, GitHub SSH access, and Pipenv for initial setup; relops installs the locked runtime dependencies. Submission needs ~/.tc_token, queue:create-task:lowest:DESTINATION (the --queue pool), queue:create-task:project:none, queue:scheduler-id:-, and every source task scope. A public task-ID --dry-run needs no token; an existing token is used if present. The interactive pool picker reads effective client scopes when credentials are present. See Replay client scopes in the linked README.

tools.name: Taskcluster task inspector
tools.description: Inspect Taskcluster task status, workers, and run timing; fetch text logs, filter lines, or output JSON.
tools.when_to_use: Use this when investigating one or more Firefox CI tasks from their IDs or Taskcluster URLs. Check the selected run's state and worker, read its text log, or filter for errors without replaying or submitting work.

beta.prerequisites: Python 3.11+, GitHub SSH access, and Pipenv for initial setup; relops installs the locked runtime dependencies. Public task summaries and public logs need no Taskcluster token. Only --auth reads clientId and accessToken from ~/.tc_token; private text artifacts require queue:get-artifact:ARTIFACT_PATH for the requested path. Help needs no credentials.
beta.note: Accepts task IDs or Firefox CI task/run URLs. --logs fetches public/logs/live_backing.log; --grep filters log lines and --artifact selects another text artifact. --run overrides the URL run; otherwise uses the URL's run or the latest. --json outputs an array. Add --auth only when credentials are needed.

tools.name: Taskcluster task creator
tools.description: Submit diagnostic tasks to a worker queue, using a timed counter or your own shell command, and optionally watch their results.
tools.when_to_use: Use a small diagnostic task to check that a worker queue accepts work, identify the worker that claims it, or run a shell command on that worker. This tool creates a fresh task rather than copying an existing Firefox CI job.

default.prerequisites: Python 3 compatible with the committed Pipfile.lock, GitHub SSH access, and Pipenv for initial setup; relops installs the locked runtime dependencies. Needs ~/.tc_token, including for --dry-run. Help does not read credentials. Submission needs permission to create tasks on the destination queue; the linked README covers usage and token setup.
default.note: --dry-run builds the request without submitting tasks, but still loads the token file.

tools.name: Taskcluster worker quarantine
tools.description: View quarantined workers, quarantine hosts, or lift their quarantine.
tools.when_to_use: Use this when investigating a worker that should be kept out of normal task scheduling, checking which workers are already quarantined, or returning a recovered worker to service. Review the target workers and their current quarantine state before changing it.

default.prerequisites: Python 3 compatible with the committed Pipfile.lock, GitHub SSH access, and Pipenv for initial setup; relops installs the locked runtime dependencies. Worker queries and quarantine actions use ~/.tc_token. Help does not read credentials. Changing quarantine needs queue:quarantine-worker permission for the target workers; the upstream README gives queue:quarantine-worker:* as an example.
default.note: The show and show-all actions also read credentials. The linked README includes token setup and examples for viewing, quarantining, and lifting quarantine.

tools.name: Moonshot oneshot tool — 24.04 X11 Talos
tools.description: Reimage and converge a Moonshot worker for Ubuntu 24.04 X11 Talos.
tools.when_to_use: Use this when preparing a Moonshot worker for Ubuntu 24.04 X11 Talos through reimaging and Puppet convergence. Review the printed plan and intended worker before confirming the operation; use the Wayland tool for a Wayland configuration.

beta.prerequisites: Bash and GitHub SSH access. Confirmed execution also needs expect, flock, ssh, nc, network access to the chassis and worker, an iLO key loaded in ssh-agent, and relops SSH/sudo access on the worker. Convergence reads scripts from ~/git/ronin_puppet and ~/vault.yaml; an optional --ronin-settings file must be readable. pv and pyfiglet are optional. relops does not prepare these system tools or files.
beta.note: Replace 229 with the desired worker. Without --confirm, prints a plan and exits. --confirm enables reimaging and convergence. See the linked runbook for iLO key setup, Ronin checkout, and SKIP_REIMAGE / SKIP_CONVERGE behavior.

tools.name: Moonshot oneshot tool — 24.04 Wayland Talos
tools.description: Reimage and converge a Moonshot worker for Ubuntu 24.04 Wayland Talos.
tools.when_to_use: Use this when preparing a Moonshot worker for Ubuntu 24.04 Wayland Talos through reimaging and Puppet convergence. Review the printed plan and intended worker before confirming the operation; use the X11 tool for an X11 configuration.

beta.prerequisites: Bash and GitHub SSH access. Confirmed execution also needs expect, flock, ssh, nc, network access to the chassis and worker, an iLO key loaded in ssh-agent, and relops SSH/sudo access on the worker. Convergence reads scripts from ~/git/ronin_puppet and ~/vault.yaml; an optional --ronin-settings file must be readable. pv and pyfiglet are optional. relops does not prepare these system tools or files.
beta.note: Replace 229 with the desired worker. Without --confirm, prints a plan and exits. --confirm enables reimaging and convergence. See the linked runbook for iLO key setup, Ronin checkout, and SKIP_REIMAGE / SKIP_CONVERGE behavior.

tools.name: Fleetroll
tools.description: Audit and monitor Firefox CI hosts, and manage their Puppet configuration.
tools.when_to_use: Use Fleetroll when auditing or monitoring a set of Firefox CI hosts, checking their Puppet configuration, or managing a configuration rollout. Choose the host operations and access needed for the investigation or change you intend to make.

default.prerequisites: Python 3.11+, GitHub SSH access, and uv for initial setup; relops installs the locked runtime dependencies. Host operations need network access, noninteractive SSH authentication, and the sudo permissions for the selected command. Taskcluster gathering and rollout reports read ~/.tc_token, or the file named by TC_TOKEN. Private GitHub comparisons need a repository-read token configured under [github] api_token in ~/.fleetroll/config.toml. The curses monitor needs a suitable terminal.
default.note: Credentials depend on the command: help needs none, and public queue counts do not need a Taskcluster token. Files listed here are used only by the relevant operations. The linked README covers host access and per-command configuration.

tools.name: Fleetbench
tools.description: Inspect host metadata or measure CPU and Android ADB transfer performance using the latest stable Fleetbench binary.
tools.when_to_use: Use Fleetbench to inspect host metadata or compare CPU performance while evaluating machines or investigating performance differences. Use its ADB transfer workload when measuring transfer performance with an attached Android device.

default.prerequisites: macOS Apple silicon or Linux amd64 and public GitHub HTTPS access for release checks/downloads. No Git, Rust, Python environment, or Taskcluster credentials are needed for inspect or cpu. The adb workload also needs adb on PATH and an attached, authorized Android device; see the linked ADB I/O instructions.
